neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech fluent without dysarthria or aphasia. MMSE 29/30 (one-point loss on delayed recall). Attention and concentration intact. No evidence of cognitive impairment beyond mild subjective memory concern the patient attributes to fatigue.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Visual acuity 20/25 right eye, 20/20 left eye. No relative afferent pupillary defect. Visual fields full to confrontation. Fundoscopic exam: mild temporal disc pallor right eye; no papilledema. Extraocular movements: horizontal nystagmus in right lateral gaze (upbeat component on upgaze). Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO): right-eye adduction lag on left lateral gaze with abducting nystagmus in left eye — consistent with right medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF) lesion. Facial sensation symmetric. Mild right facial numbness (V1-V2 distribution). Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk throughout. Mild increased tone right leg (spasticity). Strength: right hip flexion 4+/5, right knee extension 4+/5, right ankle dorsiflexion 4/5; left lower extremity 5/5 throughout; upper extremities 5/5 bilaterally. Right pronator drift present.
neurological_exam.sensory: Decreased vibration sense right lower extremity (present at ankle 6 seconds vs 14 seconds left); pinprick intact bilaterally. No dermatomal sensory level. Proprioception mildly reduced right great toe.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally. Right patellar 3+, left patellar 2+. Right Achilles 3+, left Achilles 2+. Right Babinski sign (extensor plantar response). Left plantar response flexor. Right ankle clonus: 3 beats, non-sustained.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact bilaterally. Heel-to-shin: mildly impaired right side. No intention tremor. Rapid alternating movements mildly slow right hand.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly spastic-ataxic gait with right leg circumduction. Unable to tandem walk (loses balance after two steps). Romberg sign positive (falls rightward without visual input).
neurological_exam.additional: Lhermitte sign: positive — patient reports brief electric-shock sensation into both legs on neck flexion. Uhthoff phenomenon reported: neurological symptoms transiently worsen after a hot bath.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive right leg weakness and unsteady gait over 6 weeks, now with diplopia
patient.history_present_illness: A 47-year-old right-handed Finnish male civil engineer presents to the neurology inpatient service for evaluation of subacutely progressive right leg weakness, gait unsteadiness, and new-onset horizontal diplopia over the past 6 weeks. He reports that approximately 6 weeks ago he began noticing that his right leg felt 'stiff and heavy,' initially noticeable only when climbing stairs but progressing to affect level walking. Over the ensuing 2-3 weeks he developed intermittent double vision, which he describes as horizontal and worse when looking to the left, along with a feeling of unsteadiness that prompted his wife to accompany him when walking outdoors. He endorses a positive Lhermitte sign (electric-shock sensation down both legs with neck flexion) which he first noticed 10 days ago. He also reports that his symptoms worsened noticeably after a hot bath 2 weeks ago, returning to near-baseline within an hour of cooling. He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction at present. He denies fever, weight loss, night sweats, rash, joint pains, or oral/genital ulcers. He recalls an episode approximately 8 years ago of left leg numbness lasting about 3 weeks that was attributed by a local physician to a lumbar disc herniation; he was treated with NSAIDs and physiotherapy with eventual resolution. He was not referred for brain MRI at that time. He is a former smoker (quit 7 years ago) and takes amlodipine for hypertension. His father had an ischaemic stroke at age 71, which initially led the patient and his family physician to consider a vascular aetiology for his current presentation; his BP is 136/82 on treatment. He was referred directly for inpatient neurology evaluation after his general practitioner noted asymmetric hyperreflexia and a positive Babinski sign on clinic examination.

Right juxtacortical parietal white matter, touching the cortical ribbon
Left cerebellar hemisphere, adjacent to the fourth ventricle (infratentorial)

additional_observations: Five supratentorial and infratentorial white matter lesions identified
One active enhancing lesion in right dorsal pons; four additional non-enhancing lesions in periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial regions
Simultaneous presence of enhancing and non-enhancing lesions provides MRI evidence of dissemination in time on a single scan
No cortical or subcortical mass effect
Ventricles normal in size and configuration; no hydrocephalus

mri.impression: 1. Active gadolinium-enhancing lesion in the right dorsal pons at the level of the medial longitudinal fasciculus, consistent with active demyelination. 2. Four additional non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense white matter lesions in periventricular (bilateral), juxtacortical (right parietal), and infratentorial (left cerebellar) locations. 3. Simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions fulfill MRI criteria for dissemination in time. 4. Lesion distribution (periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial) satisfies criteria for dissemination in space. Differential considerations include demyelinating disease; small-vessel ischaemic change is less consistent with the enhancing pontine lesion morphology and distribution

Oligoclonal bands: Negative — no unique CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands detected (paired serum and CSF show identical pattern). IgG index: 0.54 (normal). IgG synthesis rate: 3.8 mg/day (normal). Cytology: No malignant cells. CSF culture: No growth. CSF VDRL: Non-reactive. Myelin basic protein: 0.9 ng/mL (normal). A negative oligoclonal band result does not exclude inflammatory demyelinating disease; OCB negativity is observed in approximately 5-10% of confirmed multiple sclerosis cases

results.title: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2017 revisions of the McDonald criteria
results.authors: Thompson AJ, Banwell BL, Barkhof F, et al.
results.summary: The 2017 McDonald criteria permit MS diagnosis by MRI when DIS and DIT are met independently of CSF oligoclonal bands. Simultaneous gadolinium-enhancing and non-enhancing T2 lesions on a single MRI study constitute DIT without requiring CSF or a follow-up scan. Approximately 5-10% of clinically confirmed MS patients have negative CSF oligoclonal bands.

results.title: Multiple sclerosis
results.authors: Reich DS, Lucchinetti CF, Calabresi PA
results.summary: RRMS accounts for approximately 85-90% of newly diagnosed MS. Diagnosis rests on clinical and MRI evidence of dissemination in space and time with exclusion of alternative diagnoses. CSF oligoclonal bands support diagnosis but are neither required nor always present; false-negative rate is approximately 5-10%. High-efficacy DMTs (natalizumab, ocrelizumab, alemtuzumab, cladribine) are preferred for patients with active disease defined by clinical relapses or MRI activity.

results.title: MRI criteria for the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: MAGNIMS consensus guidelines
results.authors: Filippi M, Rocca MA, Ciccarelli O, et al.
results.summary: DIS requires lesions in at least 2 of 4 characteristic CNS regions: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord. DIT on a single scan requires simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions. Spinal cord lesions count toward both DIS and DIT criteria.

output.summary: The 2017 McDonald criteria permit RRMS diagnosis when DIS (lesions in at least 2 of 4 typical CNS regions) and DIT (including simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on a single MRI) are satisfied and alternative diagnoses are excluded. CSF oligoclonal bands substitute for DIT in one-attack presentations but are not required when MRI-based DIT criteria are fulfilled. Approximately 5-10% of confirmed MS patients have OCB-negative CSF; their absence does not exclude MS when MRI criteria are met.

output.proposed: Natalizumab 300 mg IV every 4 weeks OR ocrelizumab 600 mg IV every 6 months for relapsing-remitting MS
interactions: Amlodipine + natalizumab: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction identified
Amlodipine + ocrelizumab: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction identified
contraindications: Natalizumab: contraindicated in JC virus antibody-positive patients with high index (>0.9) due to progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) risk; JC virus serostatus must be confirmed before initiation
Natalizumab: contraindicated in active or chronic active hepatitis B infection; screen HBsAg, anti-HBc before use
Ocrelizumab: contraindicated in active HBV infection; screen before initiation
Live or live-attenuated vaccines must not be administered during or following B-cell depleting therapy
warnings: Natalizumab: requires monthly JC virus antibody index monitoring; PML risk escalates substantially with JC index >0.9 and treatment duration >2 years
Ocrelizumab: monitor for infusion-related reactions (pre-medicate with methylprednisolone, antihistamine, antipyretic); increased risk of Candida and respiratory tract infections
Both agents: do not initiate until active infections are excluded and HBV serostatus confirmed
Amlodipine: no dose adjustment required when co-administered with either agent
Monitor complete blood count at baseline and periodically during therapy
output.formulary_status: Both agents are tier 4 specialty biologics; prior authorization required; REMS programme (natalizumab TOUCH) mandatory
alternatives: Platform DMTs (interferon-beta, glatiramer acetate, teriflunomide, dimethyl fumarate) for less active disease
Cladribine (Mavenclad) oral, 2 annual courses — suitable for patients declining infusion therapy
Fingolimod (Gilenya) — requires first-dose cardiac monitoring and baseline ECG; avoid in patients with hypertension-related left ventricular hypertrophy

differential.key_features: Age 47 male with hypertension and former smoking; white matter lesions plausible on vascular basis, but active gadolinium-enhancing pontine lesion and INO are atypical for SVD; AQP4/MOG negative
Must be excluded — AQP4-IgG negative by cell-based assay; cord lesions are short-segment (not longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis ≥3 vertebral segments); makes NMOSD unlikely
MOG-IgG negative by cell-based assay; MOGAD less common in middle-aged males with a chronic relapsing course; makes MOGAD unlikely

differential.diagnosis: CNS vasculitis or lupus-related CNS disease
differential.key_features: ANA 1:80 positive — raises systemic autoimmune concern; however, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, ANCA, and complement are all normal; no systemic lupus features (rash, serositis, renal, haematological); does not meet ARA criteria for SLE-CNS
ACE normal; no cranial neuropathies beyond INO; no leptomeningeal enhancement; no systemic lymphadenopathy or pulmonary involvement; OCB-negative CSF does not favour sarcoidosis
Lyme serology (ELISA) negative; no tick exposure history; can cause multifocal white matter lesions and CSF pleocytosis (WBC here only 4), but ruled out serologically

optimal_actions.action: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI with MS protocol (FLAIR, T2, DWI, pre- and post-gadolinium T1) to assess dissemination in space and time
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in MS-typical regions (periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial); simultaneously enhancing (active) and non-enhancing lesions on the same scan satisfy MRI-based dissemination in time (McDonald 2017) — the critical finding when OCB is negative

optimal_actions.action: Extend MRI to cervical and thoracic spinal cord with contrast to identify cord lesions contributing to dissemination in space
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Short-segment (<2 vertebral bodies), peripherally located intramedullary cord lesions at C5-C6 and T4-T5 — establish cord region for DIS and distinguish from NMOSD (which produces longitudinally extensive lesions ≥3 segments)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis including oligoclonal bands (with paired serum), IgG index, cell count, protein, glucose, cytology, and VDRL
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Oligoclonal bands are NEGATIVE — this is the diagnostic puzzle; a negative result does not exclude MS (5-10% of confirmed cases are OCB-negative). DIT is already met by simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on brain MRI per McDonald 2017, so OCB negativity does not preclude the diagnosis

optimal_actions.action: Order broad mimic-exclusion serology: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, vitamin D, ANA, anti-dsDNA, complement C3/C4, AQP4-IgG (cell-based assay), MOG-IgG (cell-based assay), ANCA, ACE, HIV, RPR, Lyme serology
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG negative; ANA low-titer positive (1:80) but anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, complement, and ANCA negative — does not support CNS lupus or vasculitis; vitamin D deficient (17 ng/mL) — a comorbidity to address but not an alternative diagnosis

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for McDonald 2017 criteria including the role of MRI-based DIT when CSF oligoclonal bands are negative, and for contemporary DMT evidence in RRMS
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms that simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions satisfy DIT per McDonald 2017 without requiring OCBs; 5-10% OCB-negative MS prevalence; DMT evidence for RRMS including high-efficacy agent selection

tool_parameters.query: McDonald 2017 MS diagnosis OCB-negative oligoclonal bands MRI dissemination in time disease-modifying therapy RRMS

optimal_actions.action: Run a drug-interaction check for proposed MS DMT (natalizumab or ocrelizumab) considering existing amlodipine, JC virus risk (natalizumab), HBV screening, and live-vaccine precautions
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No clinically significant interaction with amlodipine; JC virus serology and HBV screening required before natalizumab; live vaccines contraindicated with ocrelizumab; fingolimod caution flagged given hypertension

optimal_actions.action: Obtain retinal OCT to assess RNFL and GCL thinning supporting prior subclinical right optic nerve involvement
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Marked right RNFL and GCL thinning (RNFL 74 um, temporal 51 um), consistent with prior right optic nerve axonal loss — provides structural correlate for the remote demyelinating event 8 years ago and contributes to dissemination in space (optic pathway not a formal McDonald region but supports multifocal CNS involvement)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain visual evoked potentials to document right optic pathway conduction delay
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Prolonged P100 latency right eye (124 ms) with reduced amplitude (3.1 uV) and marked interocular asymmetry (15 ms) — consistent with prior right optic nerve demyelination; provides electrophysiological evidence of a second anatomical site of involvement

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no role in MS diagnosis — findings are non-specific and do not contribute to dissemination in space or time.
CT is markedly inferior to MRI for visualising demyelinating plaques; ordering CT delays diagnosis and adds radiation without clinical benefit.
No cardioembolic indication in this MS workup; echocardiography does not inform the demyelinating differential and the normal echo fallback is expected.
Cardiac monitoring is only indicated for first-dose fingolimod initiation (bradyarrhythmia risk) — not as part of MS diagnostic workup.
FDG-PET is not indicated for MS diagnosis or DMT decisions; it does not differentiate demyelination from mimics and adds substantial cost and radiation exposure.

sequence_constraints.reason: Standard pre-LP imaging: confirm absence of mass effect or herniation risk before lumbar puncture

critical_actions: Establish dissemination in space (DIS) using brain MRI demonstrating lesions in at least 2 of 4 MS-typical regions (periventricular, juxtacortical/cortical, infratentorial, spinal cord)
Establish dissemination in time (DIT) by MRI: simultaneous gadolinium-enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on a single scan satisfy McDonald 2017 MRI-DIT independently of CSF oligoclonal band status
Recognise that negative oligoclonal bands (approximately 5-10% of confirmed MS) do not exclude MS when MRI-based DIS and DIT criteria are both independently met
Exclude NMOSD and MOGAD with cell-based assay AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG before committing to MS diagnosis and DMT selection

Perform spinal cord MRI to document cord lesion distribution: short-segment (<2 vertebral bodies), peripheral lesions distinguish MS from NMOSD (longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis ≥3 segments)
Interpret low-titer ANA (1:80) in context: anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, complement, ANCA all negative — insufficient to diagnose CNS lupus or vasculitis; does not change the MS diagnosis
Treat the acute relapse with high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3-5 days); reserve plasma exchange for steroid-refractory severe relapses

Initiate a disease-modifying therapy after relapse stabilisation; given active MRI disease with enhancing lesion, consider high-efficacy agent; obtain JC virus serostatus and HBV serology before natalizumab or ocrelizumab
Supplement vitamin D given deficiency (25-OH-D 17 ng/mL); target 40-60 ng/mL as a modifiable risk factor
contraindicated_actions: Do not exclude MS solely on the basis of negative oligoclonal bands — OCB negativity occurs in approximately 5-10% of confirmed MS; McDonald 2017 DIT can be satisfied by MRI alone (simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions)
Do not diagnose CNS lupus or vasculitis based on low-titer ANA (1:80) alone without fulfilment of SLE criteria (anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, complement consumption, systemic features — all absent here)

Do not attribute the active pontine lesion to small-vessel ischaemic disease — gadolinium enhancement in an 8 mm periventricular/infratentorial lesion without infarct diffusion pattern is not consistent with lacunar ischaemia
Do not initiate natalizumab without confirming JC virus antibody serostatus (PML risk, especially after 2 years and with JC index >0.9)
Do not administer live or live-attenuated vaccines after initiation of ocrelizumab or other B-cell depleting therapies
Do not initiate fingolimod without a baseline ECG and first-dose bradyarrhythmia monitoring; exercise caution in this patient given treated hypertension
Do not omit spinal cord MRI — cord lesion short-segment pattern is critical for excluding NMOSD and for establishing DIS
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as MS maintenance therapy — ineffective long-term and associated with significant metabolic and endocrine harm
key_reasoning_points: McDonald 2017 allows MS diagnosis by MRI-based DIT (simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on one scan) WITHOUT requiring positive CSF oligoclonal bands — the central diagnostic insight in this case
Oligoclonal band negativity (~5-10% of confirmed MS) is a well-documented phenotype; it does not alter the diagnostic threshold when MRI criteria for DIS and DIT are both independently met
DIS is met in this case across three regions: periventricular (bilateral), juxtacortical (right parietal), and infratentorial (right pons + left cerebellum); cord lesions add a fourth region

DIT is met on the initial brain MRI by simultaneous presence of the active (gadolinium-enhancing) right pontine lesion alongside four non-enhancing lesions — making a follow-up scan unnecessary for diagnosis

Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (right INO with adduction lag and contralateral abducting nystagmus) is the clinical correlate of the right dorsal pontine MLF lesion — a highly specific sign of intrinsic brainstem demyelination rarely caused by vascular disease in this distribution

Low-titer ANA (1:80 homogeneous) is a common non-specific finding in the general population; without anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, hypocomplementaemia, or systemic features, it does not support a diagnosis of CNS lupus or systemic lupus cerebritis
Mild vitamin D deficiency (17 ng/mL) is a modifiable risk factor associated with MS disease activity; it is not an alternative explanation for multifocal CNS demyelination

Short-segment (<2 vertebral segments), peripheral, dorsolateral cord lesions at C5-C6 and T4-T5 strongly favour MS over NMOSD, which produces longitudinally extensive lesions (≥3 segments) with central cord involvement
AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG must be assessed by cell-based assay (not ELISA) before committing to an MS DMT — the older ELISA-based AQP4 tests have unacceptable false-negative rates

Right optic nerve axonal loss documented by OCT (RNFL 74 um) and VEP (P100 124 ms) provides objective evidence of a prior remote demyelinating event, correlating with the self-limited left leg numbness episode 8 years ago initially misattributed to a disc herniation

red_herrings.data_point: CSF oligoclonal bands NEGATIVE (no CSF-restricted bands; paired serum and CSF identical pattern)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Agent may incorrectly conclude that negative OCBs exclude MS, abandoning the diagnosis in favour of an alternative (vascular, sarcoid, or lupus-related CNS disease)
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: OCB negativity occurs in approximately 5-10% of confirmed MS. McDonald 2017 DIT is independently satisfied by simultaneous enhancing (right pontine) and non-enhancing lesions on brain MRI; OCBs are not required for DIT when MRI criteria are met. Negative OCBs do not exclude MS.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Agent may over-interpret low-titer ANA as evidence of CNS lupus or systemic lupus-related CNS vasculitis, triggering extensive unnecessary autoimmune workup and delaying the MS diagnosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Low-titer ANA (1:80) is a non-specific finding present in up to 20-30% of the general healthy population. Anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, complement (C3 and C4), and ANCA are all negative; the patient has no systemic features of SLE (no rash, serositis, cytopenias, renal involvement). ACE is normal and there is no leptomeningeal enhancement to suggest sarcoidosis. The ANA does not meet criteria for SLE-CNS and does not alter the MS diagnosis.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Agent may attribute the multifocal neurological symptoms to vitamin D deficiency, under-investigating for demyelinating disease or incorrectly proposing supplementation as the primary intervention
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Vitamin D deficiency at this level does not cause multifocal demyelinating CNS lesions with gadolinium enhancement, INO, or Lhermitte sign. It is a modifiable comorbidity associated with MS disease activity and should be corrected, but it is not an alternative explanation for the clinical and MRI findings.

metadata.condition_name: Multiple sclerosis, relapsing-remitting type (OCB-negative, MRI-based DIT)
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: OCB-negative CSF in a 47-year-old male tempts dismissal of MS or pivot to CNS lupus (low-titer ANA) or vascular disease (hypertension, former smoker, age). The key insight is that McDonald 2017 DIT is independently satisfied by simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on a single brain MRI scan without requiring CSF oligoclonal bands. The INO provides an unmistakable brainstem demyelination signature. Three embedded red herrings (negative OCB, ANA 1:80, low vitamin D) must be correctly contextualised.
metadata.real_seed_note: Authentic case authored by condition-expert:MS-RR. No specific PMC/PMID was retrieved and verified for this exact OCB-negative RRMS presentation despite the availability of published OCB-negative MS literature. Case details are de novo and clinically consistent with the published epidemiology of OCB-negative RRMS (~5-10% prevalence per Thompson AJ et al., Lancet Neurol 2018). The OCB-negative MS phenotype is well-established in the McDonald 2017 criteria framework and confirmed by multiple observational cohorts.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools; 3 embedded red herrings (OCB negative, ANA 1:80, vitamin D deficiency); requires correct application of McDonald 2017 MRI-based DIT in the absence of CSF oligoclonal bands; multiple competing alternative diagnoses (SVD, CNS lupus, NMOSD) must be methodically excluded
case_body_concerns: Mock server note: this case has two followup_outputs using order_specialized_test (optical_coherence_tomography as initial slot, vep as secondary). Per CLINICIAN_REVIEW_FLAGS section 9 (FTD-P02/P04 note), the mock server resolves order_specialized_test to a single output slot regardless of test_type. The OCT is designated the primary slot; VEP is the secondary followup. Downstream evaluation should be aware that an agent calling both will receive OCT for the first call and VEP for the second if the mock server is updated to support multiple slots, or only OCT if not. Both are scored as recommended; neither is required.
